result.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
result.summary: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $τ^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $τ^2$-bench. ARISE-Teacher also outperforms GEPA by 4.5 pp on $τ^2$-bench and 1.4 pp on SOP-Bench. With the deployment model as its own attributor, ARISE-Self still gains 10.0 pp on SOP-Bench. ARISE-Teacher uses 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost (-1.0%).

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ARISE，一种不更新权重、工具或流程逻辑的企业 agent 记忆架构：由模型自身或教师模型归因失败并提出修正，把修正存为可检索的微记忆并整合为宏观规则，仅在留出集准确率上升时接受规则；在 SOP-Bench 与 τ²-bench 的 14 个企业流程域、5 个模型上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「失败归因→微记忆→宏观规则→留出验证门控」的更新闭环可能为 LVR 的轨迹贡献分配与推理状态监督提供借鉴，可供核查归因粒度与门控机制能否迁移到 latent 推理轨迹的修正上。
